proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 420523 reaches 1 in fewer than 383 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 383.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2948, the stopping time of n is less than 383.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 1045 modulo 19.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n*(n+1) is congruent to (n*(n+1)) + 91 modulo 13.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000 for which n^2 > 666.
The steps above establish the statement up to 2948, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 420523.
